chapter: Pianists, Basie, Lil Armstrong and closing
title: Sid Catlett's last year in Chicago and Fats and Dizzy as characters
summary: Catlett lived in his sister's building at 63rd and Ingleside before dying in 1951-52; memories of musicians as characters.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: And we were really close then. And he lived in one of my sister's buildings. He had a room there.

63rd and Ingleside. So he was living over there. And then, the day that he dropped dead was on a Easter Sunday, I think it was either '51 or '52, at a concert by Al Benson. And I told you the story about keeping the Easter egg from him. So -- see, this is the thing that's so wonderful, is all of these beautiful stories, and they crop up every now and then in your mind, and you think about this different person and that -- Louis Armstrong, and you can think about --
Pleasant memories of all these different people.
Yeah, right. Well, not only great musicians, but -- it's like I was telling you about Fats. I mean, he was more of a character offstage than he was on-stage.
